<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XII.|ACCORDING TO S. MARKE.|119 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>receiue of the husbandmen, of the fruite of the vineyard. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=3}}† Vvho apprehending him, bette him: and sent him avvay emptie. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=4}}† And againe he sent to them an other seruant: and him they vvounded in the head, and vsed him reprochefully. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=5}}† And againe he sent an other, and him they killed: and many other, beating certaine, and killing others. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=6}}† Therfore hauing yet one {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ His Sonne is {{sc|Christ}} our Sauiour, whō the Iewes crucified out of the citie of Ierusalem, as it were casting him out of the vineyard.}}∷ sonne most deere: him also he sent vnto them last saying, That they vvill reuerence my sonne. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=7}}† But the husbandmen said one to an other, This is the heier: come, let vs kill him: and the inheritance shal be ours. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=8}}† And apprehending him, they killed him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=9}}† What therfore vvil the lord of the vineyard doe? {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Iewes and their guides to whom the vineyard was set, destroied: and Gods vineyard giuen to the Apostles and their Successors in the Gentils.}}∷ He vvil come and destroy the husbandmen: and vvil giue the vineyard to others. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=10}}† Neither haue you read this scripture, ''The '' {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ {{sc|Christ}} is become the corner stone of the Synagogue and the Church in which the faithful both of the Iewes and Gentils are conteined.}}∷ ''stone vvhich the builders reiected, the same is made the head of the corner'':{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 117, 22.''}} {{verse|chapter=12|verse=11}}† ''By our Lord was this done, and it is maruelous in our eies''? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=12}}† And they sought to lay hands on him, and they feared the multitude. for they knevv that he spake this parable to them. And leauing him they vvent their vvay.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 22, 15. Lu. 26, 20.''}}* And they send to him certaine of the Pharisees and of the Herodians: that they should entrappe him in his vvord. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=14}}† VVho comming, say to him, Maister, vve knovv that thou art a true speaker, and carest not for any man: for thou doest not looke vpon the person of men, but teachest the vvay of God in truth. is it lavvful to giue tribute to Cæsar: or shal vve not giue it? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=15}}† VVho knovving their subteltie, said to them, VVhy tempt you me? bring me a penie that I may see it. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=16}}† But they brought it him. And he saith to them, VVhose is this image, and inscription? They say to him, Cæsars. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=17}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering, said to them, Render therfore the things that are Cæsars, to Cæsar: and that are Gods, {{sup|‖}} to God. And they marueled at him.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=18}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 22, 23. Lu. 20, 27. Act. 23, 6.''}}* there came to him the Saducees that say there is no resurrection: and they asked him saying, Maister, {{verse|chapter=12|verse=19}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 25, 5.''}}* Moyses vvrote vnto vs, that if any mans brother die, and leaue his vvife, and leaue no children, {{sup|‖}} his brother shal take his vvife and raise vp seede to his brother. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=20}}† There vvere therfore seuen brethren: and the first tooke a vvife, and died leauing no issue. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=21}}† And the second tooke her, and died: and neither this left issue. And the third in like maner. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=22}}† And the seuen tooke her in like sort: and did not leaue issue. Last of al the vvoman also<noinclude>{{rh|||died.}}</noinclude>
